text:
raj: Heads-up — we started a canary rollout of the CUDA 12.2 base image + nvidia-container-toolkit 1.9 to us-west GPU nodes and some GPU pods are failing to start.

maria: Seeing crashloops on embeddings-canary in us-west-2. Error inside container: 'could not load libcuda.so.1: file not found'. Containers end up without /run/nvidia/driver populated. :eyes:

jason: Same. Kubelet logs show the host /run/nvidia/driver is present but inside the container it's empty. Looks like the hostPath bind didn't propagate.

infra-bot: deploy: canary completion failed (12/50 pods failed)

sylvie: Any quick workaround before we pause the rollout? Revert the image?

raj: Short-term workaround: set mountPropagation: Bidirectional on GPU pod HostPath mounts for /run/nvidia. That lets the pod see the host symlink targets. Also pausing rollout now. Reverting the canary image is safest.

jason: Repro steps: 
```
# host
ls -la /run/nvidia/driver
lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root 42 Mar 15 10:22 /run/nvidia/driver -> /var/lib/nvidia/driver-20260315-7b9c

# inside container
ls -la /run/nvidia/driver
ls: cannot access '/run/nvidia/driver': No such file or directory

# error
nvidia-smi: could not load NVML library: libnvidia-ml.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

maria: We ran a quick docker run with nvidia/cuda:12.2-base on one node and reproduced the NVML load error. If the symlink target lives under /var/lib and the runtime mounts snapshots in a different order, the symlink ends up dangling inside the container.

raj: Root cause hypothesis: toolkit 1.9 now creates driver layout where /run/nvidia/driver is a symlink to a versioned dir under /var/lib/nvidia. Container runtimes with certain mount propagation and snapshotter ordering end up with the symlink resolved on the host but not visible inside container namespaces. Vendor changelog hints at lifecycle changes.

sylvie: Is this the bind-propagation regression the vendor mentioned in their release notes?

jason: Vendor confirmed via support that 1.9 introduced a regression in how tmpfiles and symlink targets are created; they have a patch incoming but no ETA yet. We've opened INC-9421 with vendor and marked P2.

maria: Proposed plan: 1) Pause 12.2 rollout immediately. 2) Revert canary to 12.1 for now. 3) Cordon/evict affected nodes in us-west-2 and replace with nodes running 12.1. 4) Bake node-image with toolkit 1.8/1.9 pinned depending on vendor patch. 5) Add an e2e node check that verifies /run/nvidia/driver exists and contains a real nvml lib.

raj: I'm pushing a temporary DaemonSet that will restart the nvidia-container-toolkit service and apply a bind-mount fix for existing pods. Also a quick remediation: restart containerd after toolkit restart on affected nodes. Not ideal but unblocks most workloads.

jason: Example snippet to add to pod spec (eng-infra runbook):
```
volumeMounts:
  - name: nvidia-run
    mountPath: /run/nvidia
    mountPropagation: Bidirectional
volumes:
  - name: nvidia-run
    hostPath:
      path: /run/nvidia
      type: Directory
```

sylvie: Impact summary: ~12 nodes in us-west-2 affected, roughly 10% reduced GPU capacity for the pool. Cost impact minimal short-term but paging SRE if node failures exceed 5.

infra-bot: incident created INC-9421 assigned to raj, severity P2

raj: Adding vendor PR link and rollback PR to the incident. Rolling back the canary now and will coordinate full rollback at 18:30 UTC. Follow-up: add node-level validation and CI gate to catch symlink/mount propagation regressions for future toolkit upgrades.

maria: Thanks everyone — pausing rollout and posting the revert PR in #eng-releases. :thumbsup:
